title: Determinant under pivot elimination
statement: Let $p$ be prime, let $v$ be a list of natural numbers and let $R$ be a list of rows, with $v$ having length $|R|+1$ and every row in $R$ having length $|R|+1$. Suppose the first entry of $v$, reduced modulo $p$, is nonzero, and let $u$ be a natural number whose residue modulo $p$ is the inverse of that first entry. Then the determinant over $ br/p br$ of the matrix with rows $v$ followed by $R$ equals the first entry of $v$ modulo $p$ times the determinant of the matrix formed from the rows obtained by eliminating the pivot using $u$.
hypotheses_covered: The first entry of $v$, reduced modulo $p$, is nonzero.
The residue of $u$ modulo $p$ is the multiplicative inverse of the first entry of $v$ modulo $p$.
